headline: Winds up to 150kmph: Cyclone Arnab becomes very severe as 4 ports warned
summary: The Meteorological Department has issued Signal 3 for Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports as the storm intensifies in the Bay of Bengal.
details: Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, according to a special bulletin issued by the Meteorological Department on Tuesday afternoon.
As of 12 PM on Tuesday, the storm was located southwest of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports, with distances ranging from 965km to 1,130km.
The storm is moving west-northwest and is expected to cross the Andhra coast of India by Wednesday afternoon, October 28.
Maximum sustained wind speeds within 64km of the storm's center are 130kmph, rising to 150kmph in gusts or squalls.
The Meteorological Department has advised fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal to remain cautious and operate only near the coast until further notice.
Local warning signal number 3 has been hoisted at the four sea ports of Bangladesh to ensure safety and preparedness.

headline: HSC results delayed to October 31
summary: The publication date for Higher Secondary Certificate and equivalent exams has been revised from October 29 to October 31.
details: The publication date for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exam results has been pushed back. According to the new decision, the results will now be published on October 31 instead of October 29.
Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, Chairman of the Dhaka Education Board and President of the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the news on Tuesday.
This year's HSC and equivalent exams began on July 2 and concluded on September 9.
Across the country, 1,270,583 students from 9,439 educational institutions under 11 education boards participated in the exams.
There were 2,697 examination centers nationwide for these students.
Additionally, 92,905 students took the exams at 461 centers under the Madrasah Education Board, and 107,964 students at 610 centers under the Technical Education Board.
